Assessment.content: Acute infectious gastroenteritis suspected, likely viral, based on abrupt onset, vomiting, watery-to-loose stools, abdominal pain, and contact with ill household member
Assessment.source_text: 1) Acute infectious gastroenteritis suspected (likely viral) given abrupt onset, vomiting, watery-to-loose stools, abdominal pain, and contact with ill household member.

Assessment.content: Dehydration risk suspected due to persistent vomiting and poor oral intake; currently passing urine but hydration status requires assessment
Assessment.source_text: 2) Dehydration risk suspected due to persistent vomiting and poor oral intake; currently able to urinate (urine once an hour ago) but hydration status requires assessment.

Assessment.content: Symptoms described as compatible with infectious gastroenteritis and most cases are self-limiting, but stool test needed to exclude bacterial cause
Assessment.source_text: Brief explanation: symptoms compatible with infectious gastroenteritis; most cases self-limiting but stool test needed to exclude bacterial cause.

Plan_of_Care.content: Urgent clinic appointment arranged for hydration assessment and stool sample
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Urgent clinic appointment arranged for hydration assessment and stool sample.

Plan_of_Care.content: Stool sample planned to rule out bacterial infection needing targeted therapy
Plan_of_Care.source_text: – Stool sample to rule out bacterial infection needing targeted therapy.

Plan_of_Care.content: In-clinic visit preferred so stool sample can be sent promptly; if not feasible, sample to be posted
Plan_of_Care.source_text: – In-clinic visit preferred so sample can be sent promptly; if not feasible, sample to be posted.

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue oral rehydration salts and take very small, frequent sips to minimize vomiting
Plan_of_Care.source_text: – Continue oral rehydration salts; take very small, frequent sips to minimize vomiting.

Plan_of_Care.content: If able to keep fluids down, gradually reintroduce clear fluids and light foods such as toast or biscuits
Plan_of_Care.source_text: – If able to keep down, gradually reintroduce clear fluids and light foods (toast/biscuits);

Plan_of_Care.content: Avoid dairy and raw fruits and vegetables initially

Monitor for signs of dehydration or worsening illness and seek urgent care (A&E) if vomiting persists with inability to keep any fluids down, confusion, persistent high fever, severe abdominal pain, or reduced urine output
Plan_of_Care.source_text: – Monitor for signs of dehydration or worsening illness; seek urgent care (A&E) if vomiting persists unable to keep any fluids down, confusion, persistent high fever, severe abdominal pain, or reduced urine output.

Plan_of_Care.content: Education provided that symptoms are compatible with infectious gastroenteritis, most cases are self-limiting, and stool test is needed to exclude bacterial cause

Plan_of_Care.content: If more unwell prior to appointment, advised to present to A&E
